messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: potential cross-tenant KV read detected (severity: high) — affected: customer Polaris (cust-918), deployment: vpc-dedicated gp-5, symptom: anomalous get on namespace 'polaris/2026-prod' returning keys from 'zephyr' namespace. Triggered at 2026-03-15T09:07:14Z. Paging oncall.

Ava (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledging pager. @Ravi @Marta please standby for quick isolation.

Ravi (SRE): @Ava can you paste the raw alert? want the full query + backend node IDs.

Ava (oncall): alert payload: ``ALERT_ID=kb-4938; NODE=gp-5-n3; OP=get; NAMESPACE=polaris/2026-prod; RETURNED_PREFIX=zephyr/; SAMPLE_KEY=zephyr/user-9321/profile``

Marta (Infra): gp-5-n3 is in AZ-west-2b, dedicated pool. Running quick kvtrace on node now.

Ava (oncall): Elijah / Jenna can you confirm whether Polaris reported anything? Elijah?

Elijah (Customer Eng): Haven't heard from Polaris yet. I'm drafting outreach but holding until we confirm impact. If keys from another tenant were visible that's PII-risk.

Ravi (SRE): Running quick check: ``SELECT count(*) FROM kv_access_logs WHERE node='gp-5-n3' AND ts > '2026-03-15T08:50:00Z' AND key LIKE 'zephyr/%'``

Ravi (SRE): result: 7 reads from internal health-checks and 2 API GETs from polaris-prod clients. Need to know whether those GETs returned zephyr payloads or just metadata.

Marta (Infra): KV process logs: ``[09:06:58] prefix-resolve fallback: matched ambiguous-prefix 'ze' -> resolved to polaris/2026-prod (priority tie)`` looks like prefix disambiguation picked wrong namespace mapping on that node.

Ava (oncall): Sounds like namespace-prefix collision on that node's routing table. Possible stale cache. Recommended immediate mitigation: 1) move polaris traffic off gp-5-n3 2) evict node from pool 3) scrub node cache. Can we route polaris to gp-5-n2?

Marta (Infra): I can remove gp-5-n3 from the dedicated pool and re-route. Doing `infractl pool evict --pool gp-5 --node gp-5-n3 --reason "tenant-prefix-collision"` now.

PagerDuty: Acknowledged by Ava (oncall) at 2465001236.

Ava (oncall): After eviction, confirm client successes and whether any GETs still returning cross-tenant keys.

Marta (Infra): Eviction completed at 09:11:04Z. Traffic for polaris shifted to gp-5-n2.

Ravi (SRE): Re-running the log query for returned payloads. ``grep -A2 "SVC-GET" /var/log/kv/gp-5-n3/access.log | grep zephyr`` -> shows 2 payload dumps that include user emails and hashed tokens.

Ava (oncall): That's bad. Elijah/Jenna we should prepare notification draft. Jenna, open a high-priority SEV communication.

Jenna (Customer Support): I'll start templated outreach: acknowledging incident, we are investigating possible exposure, will update in 2 hours. Do you have firm list of impacted keys?

Ravi (SRE): Extracting keys now. Found 5 unique keys that returned zephyr/* objects to polaris callers. Keys: ``zephyr/user-9321/profile``, ``zephyr/session-13AB/token``, ``zephyr/settings/org-77`` (truncated).

Marta (Infra): Initiating node scrub and KV cache invalidation on gp-5-n3. Running: ``systemctl stop redwood-kv && rm -rf /var/lib/kv/cache/* && systemctl start redwood-kv``. Starting scrub job and orbiting to forensic storage.

Ava (oncall): Also please snapshot the node disk and attach to case. We need raw evidence for postmortem and customer Q/A.

Marta (Infra): Snapshot started. ETA ~8m.

Elijah (Customer Eng): I'm drafting a targeted notification for Polaris. Need timeline of requests and confirmation whether data persisted in their replication streams.

Ravi (SRE): Quick check: no writes observed from polaris clients to zephyr keys; only reads returned misrouted data. Ring-fencing: no downstream replication to polaris because our routing layer prevents cross-namespace writes, but we need to confirm whether any telemetry or logs leaked to polaris exports.

Ava (oncall): Action items: 1) Marta: complete scrub + snapshot (in progress) 2) Ravi: full audit of access logs for gp-5-n3 for last 24h + identify any other nodes with stale prefix tables 3) Elijah/Jenna: customer outreach template + live sync with Polaris CSM 4) SRE rotation: handoff to Ravi at 09:30Z for longer triage.

Ravi (SRE): I'll take the handoff at 09:30Z. For now running cluster-wide check for ambiguous-prefix entries: ``for n in gp-5-*; do ssh $n \"grep -H 'ambiguous-prefix' /var/log/kv/*\"; done``

Marta (Infra): scrub finished and node snapshot attached to ticket #INC-2026-918. Cache invalidation logs uploaded to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/2026/INC-2026-918/`.

Jenna (Customer Support): Polaris CSM is on standby. Draft sent to legal for review before outbound. Recommend not calling customer until we have confirmed scope.

Elijah (Customer Eng): Notifying Polaris CSM now with acknowledgement. Will request timebox meeting after we confirm scopes.

Ravi (SRE): cluster-wide scan shows 2 other nodes with stale prefix-tables in gp-5 (gp-5-n7 had a similar ambiguous-prefix event but no cross-tenant reads). We're scheduling rolling cache refresh across pool (non-disruptive).

Ava (oncall): Handoff note: I'm leaving triage to Ravi at 09:30Z. If pages escalate re: customer impact, page SRE lead.

IncidentBot: Handoff recorded — previous oncall: Ava (oncall); new oncall: Ravi (SRE); handoff_ts=2465001400.

Ravi (SRE): Initial mitigation complete: evicted node, scrubbed, snapshot taken, customer contacted for opt-in call. Next steps: 1) complete key-level exposure assessment 2) run forensics across gp-5 for last 72h 3) prepare mitigation/remediation runbook (prefix-disambiguation fix + validation tests).

Jenna (Customer Support): Confirmed Polaris escalation channel open. We'll coordinate postmortem and customer Q/A after full scope.

Elijah (Customer Eng): Quick note for postmortem: add unit that explains dedicated pool prefix collision and caching TTL semantics — likely root cause.

Ravi (SRE): I'll keep updates here. Current status: mitigation applied, suspicious returns found (5 keys), snapshot and scrub done, customer notified. Moving to investigative phase.

Ava (oncall): Thx team. Leaving channel. :white_check_mark:
